mil3.1.3:1.2: “Venerable Nāgasena, will you converse with me?”
mil3.1.3:1.3: “If you, Great King, converse in the manner of the wise, I will converse; but if you converse in the manner of kings, I will not converse.”
mil3.1.3:1.4: “How, Venerable Nāgasena, do the wise converse?”
mil3.1.3:1.5: “In the conversation of the wise, Great King, both entangling and disentangling are done, both refutation and correction are done, both trust and trust in return are done, and the wise do not get angry because of it. That, Great King, is how the wise converse.”
mil3.1.3:1.6: “But how, venerable sir, do kings converse?”
mil3.1.3:1.7: “In conversation, Great King, kings insist on one position, and whoever contradicts that position, they order punishment for him: ‘Impose a penalty on this man!’ That, Great King, is how kings converse.”
mil3.1.3:1.8: “I, venerable sir, will converse in the manner of the wise, not in the manner of kings. Let the Reverend converse freely; just as he would converse with a mendicant, a novice, a lay follower, or a monastery attendant, so let the Reverend converse freely; do not be afraid.”
